BudgetWise is a .NET 8 ASP.NET Core Web API with a React/TypeScript/Vite/Tailwind frontend for personal finance, used in the GitHub Copilot Workshop.

**Code:** Follow C# PascalCase and camelCase conventions; use descriptive names, focused methods, composition, C# 12 where appropriate, `var` when types are obvious, and `using` inside namespaces. Use TypeScript with strict typing; React hooks, functional, focused/reusable components, Tailwind, semantic HTML, accessibility, and no inline styles. Use constructor dependency injection and appropriate service lifetimes. Use consistent minimal APIs or controllers; RESTful nouns/HTTP methods, typed results or `IActionResult`, validation, middleware, explicit domain/DTO mapping, and immutable `record` DTOs. Add validation annotations and XML docs to public classes/methods (`<summary>`, `<param>`, `<returns>`, `<exception>` where applicable); comments explain why. Mark incomplete features `// TODO:` with a clear description.

**Tests:** Use xUnit and React Testing Library; AAA; descriptive `MethodName_WhenCondition_ThenExpectedResult` names; `WebApplicationFactory<T>` for integration tests; mock external dependencies/API calls with MSW or similar. Cover success/failure, edges/boundaries, accessibility, and user interactions; use Testing Library `screen` queries.

**API/data:** Use GET/POST/PUT/DELETE appropriately; plural resource paths, IDs as path variables, filters as query parameters; appropriate status codes, meaningful errors, camelCase JSON, and Content-Type headers. Use DTOs for complex payloads and validate with Data Annotations or FluentValidation. Use realistic in-memory development/test data from `MockData` in `Data/MockData.cs`; thread-safe collections where needed. Models use property-based initialization, navigation properties, appropriate nullable references, and `required` for mandatory properties.

Check existing patterns; follow ASP.NET and frontend conventions; include error handling, tests, documentation, validation, typed responses, and full-stack coherence. When implementing workshop TODOs, follow existing patterns, test features, and update documentation. Prefer clarity and beginner-friendly simplicity; demonstrate best practices and explain .NET Core/React concepts.

❌ Do not use service locator pattern (always use dependency injection)
❌ Do not return null from API endpoints (use `NotFound()` or throw exceptions)
❌ Do not put business logic in controllers (use services)
❌ Do not ignore exceptions or use empty catch blocks
❌ Do not use `any` type in TypeScript (use proper types or `unknown`)
❌ Do not create side effects in React component render functions

**Commands**
```sh
cd budgetwise-app/backend
dotnet restore              # Restore dependencies
dotnet build                # Build the project
dotnet run                  # Start the API server (port 5000)
dotnet test                 # Run tests
dotnet watch run            # Run with hot reload
cd budgetwise-app/frontend
npm install                 # Install dependencies
npm run dev                 # Start dev server with Vite (port 5173)
npm run build               # Production build
npm run preview             # Preview production build
npm run lint                # Run ESLint
npm run test                # Run tests
```

**Project paths**
- `budgetwise-app/backend/Program.cs` — entry point and middleware
- `budgetwise-app/backend/Controllers/` — REST endpoints
- `budgetwise-app/backend/Models/` — domain models and DTOs
- `budgetwise-app/backend/Services/` — business logic
- `budgetwise-app/backend/Data/MockData.cs` — mock data
- `budgetwise-app/frontend/src/App.tsx` — main React app
- `budgetwise-app/frontend/src/services/api.ts` — API client
- `budgetwise-app/frontend/src/types/index.ts` — TypeScript types
- `budgetwise-app/README.md` — project documentation
